<reason>A wins the regulatory-design comparison. It directly answers who pays and how conventional crops are treated, then explains how published risk-based criteria remove irrelevant burdens upfront while preserving targeted testing. B establishes a plausible case against redundant regulation, but its comparative advantage depends on recasting A's proposal as requiring full dossiers, litigated waivers, or worldwide reform. A also identifies that B's full-review escalation can impose more burdens than testing the particular unresolved hazard.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>A's second rebuttal dismantles B's “toll booth” argument: necessary testing remains under both proposals, while predictable eligibility rules need not require litigated waivers. B's allegation that A left its questions unanswered was also premature—the scheduled answering turn had not yet occurred, and A subsequently answered both directly.</best_rebuttal>
